'''Gathorne Gathorne-Hardy, 5th Earl of Cranbrook''' (20 June 1933 – 24 August 2026), styled '''Lord Medway''' until 1978, was a British [[zoologist]], biologist, [[naturalist]] and [[Peerages in the United Kingdom|peer]].<ref name="burke">{{cite book |title=[[Burke's Peerage|Burke's Peerage, Baronetage & Knighthood]] |publisher=Burke's Peerage & Gentry |editor=Mosley, Charles |editor-link=Charles Mosley (genealogist) |edition=107 |year=2003 |page=941 |ref=Burke |isbn=0-9711966-2-1}}</ref> From 1956 to his death in 2026, he was active in the fields of [[ornithology]], [[mammalogy]], and [[zooarchaeology]], and influenced research and education in [[Southeast Asia]].<ref name="rhino">{{cite journal |title=Cranbrook at 80: Cranbrook at Eighty: His Contributions So Far. Ornithologist, Mammalogist, Zooarchaeologist, Chartered Biologist and Naturalist |journal=The Raffles Bulletin of Zoology Supplement |date=2013 |issue=29 |pages=1–7 |url=http://www.rhinoresourcecenter.com/pdf_files/139/1396264267.pdf}}</ref> His career focus was on [[swiftlet]]s and other small Southeast Asian birds, as well as on mammals, including [[orangutan]]s.<ref name="thestar">{{cite news |last1=Ying |first1=Lim Chia |title=Lifelong commitment to nature |url=https://www.thestar.com.my/lifestyle/people/2014/11/17/lifelong-commitment-to-nature/ |access-date=18 March 2019 |work=The Star |date=17 November 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hance |first=Jeremy |date=2017-03-02 |title=David Attenborough attacks plan for Borneo bridge that threatens orangutans |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2017/mar/02/david-attenborough-attacks-plan-for-borneo-bridge |access-date=2023-04-06 |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mattle-Greminger |first1=Maja P. |last2=Bilgin Sonay |first2=Tugce |last3=Nater |first3=Alexander |last4=Pybus |first4=Marc |last5=Desai |first5=Tariq |last6=de Valles |first6=Guillem |last7=Casals |first7=Ferran |last8=Scally |first8=Aylwyn |last9=Bertranpetit |first9=Jaume |last10=Marques-Bonet |first10=Tomas |last11=van Schaik |first11=Carel P. |last12=Anisimova |first12=Maria |last13=Krützen |first13=Michael |date=2018-11-15 |title=Genomes reveal marked differences in the adaptive evolution between orangutan species |journal=Genome Biology |volume=19 |issue=1 |pages=193 |doi=10.1186/s13059-018-1562-6 |issn=1474-760X |pmc=6237011 |pmid=30428903 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Cranbrook was the author of ''Wild Mammals of South-East Asia'' (1986), ''Wonders of nature in South-East Asia'' (1997) and ''Swiftlets of Borneo: Builders of Edible Nests'' (2002) and ''Key Environments: Malaysia'' (2013), which had a foreword from [[Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=YING |first=LIM CHIA |title=Lifelong commitment to nature |url=https://www.thestar.com.my/lifestyle/people/2014/11/17/lifelong-commitment-to-nature |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=The Star |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Environmental leading light, Lord Cranbrook, rewarded for work by Duke of Edinburgh |url=https://www.eadt.co.uk/news/21697564.environmental-leading-light-lord-cranbrook-rewarded-work-duke-edinburgh/ |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=East Anglian Daily Times |date=17 November 2014 |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and career==
Cranbrook was born in London, the eldest child of [[John Gathorne-Hardy, 4th Earl of Cranbrook]], an archaeologist and also a zoologist, and his second wife, Fidelity Seebohm, daughter of Hugh Exton Seebohm and sister of [[Frederic Seebohm, Baron Seebohm|Lord Seebohm]]. He was educated at [[Eton College]] and [[Corpus Christi College, Cambridge]]. Cranbrook attended Cambridge at the same time as his cousin, the writer and biographer [[Jonathan Gathorne-Hardy]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Bx7W-uJ10uoC&dq=Jonathan+Gathorne-Hardy+May+17%2C++1933&pg=PA147 |title=Half an Arch: A Memoir |isbn=9781857252019 |last=Gathorne-Hardy |first=Jonathan |year=2004 |page=147}}</ref> He earned his PhD in 1960 from the [[University of Birmingham]].<ref name="burke" />

A tropical biologist,<ref name="DID">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b00kmndy |title=Desert Island Discs - Castaway : Caroline, Countess of Cranbrook |work=[[BBC Online]] |publisher=BBC |access-date=18 August 2014}}</ref> Cranbrook worked in [[Peninsular Malaysia|Malaya]], beginning his career as an assistant at [[Sarawak Museum]], Sarawak.<ref>{{Cite web |title=National University of Singapore: Earl of Cranbrook |url=https://lkcnhm.nus.edu.sg/scientist-feature-earl-of-cranbrook/ |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=lkcnhm.nus.edu.sg}}</ref> He was a senior lecturer in zoology between 1961 and 1970 at [[University of Malaya|University of Malaya, Kuala Lumpur]], and a Jajason Siswa Lokantara Fellow between 1960 and 1961 at Indonesia.<ref>{{Cite web |title=WWF honours lifelong commitment to nature |url=https://wwf.panda.org/wwf_news/?232873/WWF-honours-lifelong-commitment-to-nature |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=wwf.panda.org |language=en}}</ref> After many years working in the far-east, he returned with his wife [[Caroline, Countess of Cranbrook|Caroline Cranbrook]] and young family to take up residence at his family seat, Glemham House, [[Great Glemham]], near Saxmundham, Suffolk.<ref name="Surman">{{cite web |url=http://www.farmersguardian.com/home/rural-life/profile-lady-caroline-cranbrook/30448.article |title=Profile: Lady Caroline Cranbrook |last=Surman |first=William |date=26 February 2010 |work=[[Farmers Guardian]] |access-date=20 August 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714165512/http://www.farmersguardian.com/home/rural-life/profile-lady-caroline-cranbrook/30448.article |archive-date=14 July 2014 }}</ref>

He succeeded as [[Earl of Cranbrook]] upon his father's death in 1978, and sat as a [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] peer in the [[House of Lords]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.parliament.uk/biographies/Lords/member/3382 |title=Parliamentary career for Earl of Cranbrook - MPS and Lords - UK Parliament}}</ref> He left the Lords in November 1999 as a result of the [[House of Lords Act 1999]]; he was not a candidate to retain a place in the House as an [[List of excepted hereditary peers|elected hereditary peer]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.election.demon.co.uk/lords.html |title=House of Lords Act: Hereditary Peers Elections |website=Election Demon |last1=Boothroyd |first1=David |archive-date=30 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190730022405/http://www.election.demon.co.uk/lords.html |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Cranbrook was awarded the [[Gold Medal (RGS)|Royal Geographical Founders Gold Medal]] and the [[World Wildlife Fund|WWF]] Duke of Edinburgh Conservation Award in recognition of his work in UK and Tropical Nature Conservation and Research. He was created [[Most Exalted Order of the Star of Sarawak|Panglima Negara Bintang Sarawak (Knight Commander of the Most Exalted Order of the Star of Sarawak)]] and received the Merdeka Award recognising his outstanding contribution to the people of Malaysia.

A species of [[white-toothed shrew]], [[Gathorne's shrew]] (''Crocidura gathornei''), is named in his honor.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Jenkins |first=Paula D. |date=2013 |title=An account of the Himalayan mountain soricid community, with the description of a new species of ''Crocidura'' (Mammalia: Soricomorpha: Soricidae) |url=https://lkcnhm.nus.edu.sg/wp-content/uploads/sites/10/app/uploads/2017/06/s29rbz161-175.pdf |journal=Raffles Bulletin of Zoology |volume=Suppl.29 |pages=161–175}}</ref>

==Marriage and issue==
On 9 May 1967, he married [[Caroline, Countess of Cranbrook|Caroline Jarvis]], daughter of Col. Ralph Jarvis and his wife Antonia ''née'' Meade, a scion of the [[Earl of Clanwilliam]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Mosley |first=Charles |title=Burke's Peerage, Baronetage & Knightage |publisher=Burke's Peerage (Genealogical Books) Ltd |year=2003 |edition=107 |volume=3}}</ref>
Cranbrook and his wife had three children:<ref name="burke"/>

* John Jason Gathorne-Hardy, 6th Earl of Cranbrook (born 26 October 1968), born in [[Kuala Lumpur]].<ref name="DID"/>
* Lady Flora Gathorne-Hardy (born 10 October 1971).
* [[The Honourable|Hon.]] Argus Edward Gathorne-Hardy (born 28 May 1973), [[heir presumptive]] to his brother.

==Death==
Gathorne-Hardy died on 24 August 2026, aged 93.<ref>[https://www.theborneopost.com/2026/08/27/earl-of-cranbrook-gathorne-gathorne-hardy-passes-away-at-age-93/ Earl of Cranbrook Gathorne Gathorne-Hardy passes away at age 93]</ref>
